query: How can melting temperature, enthalpy and entropy of fusion, volume change at melting, and liquid-phase thermodynamic properties be determined accurately and efficiently across the high-entropy-alloy family? State the physical rationale, expected quantitative performance, range of applicability, supporting prior evidence, and a decisive validation result that would rule out the proposed approach.

generation.hypothesis: High-Resolution DSC-Synchrotron XRD Coupling for Accurate Fusion Property Determination in HEAs
generation.material_initial_state: Bulk vacuum induction melted and homogenized HEA samples (both equiatomic and non‐equiatomic, e.g., a representative Cantor alloy and refractory Nb-Mo-Ta-W-V alloy)
generation.intervention: Apply controlled heating (e.g., 10 K/min) using high-sensitivity DSC/DTA simultaneously with in-situ synchrotron XRD measurements
generation.conditions: Inert atmosphere (Ar or N2) with a temperature ramp from room temperature to above the melting point; calibrated using well-known standards
generation.structural_mediator: Transition from crystalline solid to liquid state marked by abrupt changes in heat capacity and lattice parameter shifts detected by XRD
generation.mechanism: Integration of heat flow data (via DSC) with structural changes (from XRD) allows direct calculation of melting temperature, latent heat (enthalpy), entropy changes (via integrated cp curves), and volume changes at melting
generation.predicted_outcome: Fusion enthalpy and entropy values will be determined with an uncertainty of ±5–10% and melting temperature resolved within ±5 K; volume changes measured within ±2% relative to baseline standards
generation.baseline: Calibrated measurements on pure metals (e.g., Ni) and previously established DSC data (see PMC7513177::web::004::1_introduction)
generation.boundary: Approach is best applicable to HEAs with relatively homogeneous microstructures; complexities from severe segregation or multiphase mixtures may degrade accuracy
generation.uncertainty: Uncertainties arise from instrument resolution, thermal lag at high heating rates, and potential sample inhomogeneity

falsification_experiment.design: Perform DSC and in-situ synchrotron XRD on a benchmark HEA sample with known fusion properties; compare the measured melting temperature, fusion enthalpy, and volume change to established literature values
measurements: Derived fusion entropy from integrated cp curves
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the extracted melting temperature deviates by more than 5% or fusion enthalpy/volume change measurements differ by more than 10% from baseline values, the approach is invalidated

During heating (red curve), two distinct endothermic peaks are observed. The first peak starts at 1113.7 K, reaches a maximum at 1201.7 K, and ends at 1228.1 K, with an absorbed energy of −10.1 J/g. The second, more intense endothermic peak begins at 1297.7 K and ends at 1327.2 K, corresponding to the melting process, with an energy absorption of −70.53 J/g. During cooling (blue curve), two exothermic peaks appear, indicating crystallization processes. The first peak starts at 1126.6 K, reaches a maximum at 1154.0 K, and ends at 1198.9 K, with a released energy of −9.1 J/g. The second, more pronounced exothermic peak begins at 1198.9 K, reaches a maximum at 1297.2 K, and ends at 1305.9 K, releasing −48.3 J/g, suggesting the crystallization of the primary phase from the liquid.

The calculation of configurational entropy, also called mixing entropy, is given in Equation (3) with n as the number of elements, xi the concentration of each element i and R as the universal gas constant. The equation is derived from the mixing of noble gases and is adopted to fully disordered solid solution, which are assumed in our work. If elements are distributed non-equally between possible sub-lattices, then a more general equation should be used []. In case of an equiatomic alloy, Equation (3) is reduced to ΔSconf=Rlnn. Thus the configurational entropy of 5-component equiatomic alloy is ~1.6·R. At 0 K the resulting total entropy may not be zero. This does not violate the third law of thermodynamics (dSdT|T=0=0) which is often misinterpreted as S(T = 0) = 0. Crystalline solids may exhibit a non-zero entropy at the absolute zero point due to a randomly crystallographic orientation. A change of entropy in this point is not possible, because there is no ability of motion or diffusion. papers.title: How atoms of polycrystalline Nb20.6Mo21.7Ta15.6W21.1V21.0 refractory high-entropy alloys rearra
papers.system: Refractory high-entropy alloys (Nb-Mo-Ta-W-V) in both single-crystal and polycrystalline forms
papers.approach: Molecular dynamics (MD) simulations using a 2NN MEAM potential; analysis of density profiles, enthalpy evolution, and grain size effects
papers.findings: Observed an abrupt change in density and enthalpy around 2910–2940 K indicating local structural rearrangements. In polycrystalline samples, a two-stage melting process was reported: initial pre-melting of grain boundary regions followed by full melting, with the melting point showing logarithmic growth with increasing grain size.
papers.mechanism: Melting occurs via collective atomic rearrangements—initially at grain boundaries (premelting) and then across the bulk. The simulation provides an empirical relation between grain size and melting point.

papers.title: Entropy Determination of Single-Phase High Entropy Alloys with Different Crystal Structures over a Wide Temperature Range.
papers.system: Single-phase high-entropy alloys (various crystal structures: fcc, bcc, hcp) including equiatomic systems
papers.approach: Experimental determination of temperature-dependent heat capacity cp(T) via differential scanning calorimetry (DSC) from low temperatures up to the solidus temperature
papers.findings: Demonstrated that thermal entropy (from cp measurements) is the dominant contribution compared to configurational entropy, with cp values consistent with the Dulong–Petit law at room temperature. Provided a quantitative framework linking measured heat capacities to total entropy.
papers.mechanism: Based on the Debye T³ law at low temperatures and equipartition at higher temperatures, linking thermal fluctuations to measurable cp and thereby to thermal entropy and indirectly to enthalpic contributions.

papers.title: Computational property predictions of Ta-Nb-Hf-Zr high-entropy alloys.
papers.approach: Hybrid Monte Carlo/Molecular Dynamics (MC/MD) simulations to evolve the structure and calculate thermodynamic quantities such as ΔH and ΔG over annealing treatment at 1800 °C
papers.findings: Identified a gradual reduction in Gibbs free energy with significant contributions from configurational entropy once local chemical clustering develops; convergence in ΔG observed after ~20 MC swaps, evidencing thermodynamic equilibrium.
papers.mechanism: Local chemical ordering deviates from ideal randomness, affecting both enthalpy and entropy. The interplay between atomic swaps (MC) and thermal relaxations (MD) captures the balance between energetic and entropic contributions.

papers.title: Predictive multiphase evolution in Al-containing high-entropy alloys.
papers.system: Al-containing high-entropy alloys with multiphase microstructures
papers.approach: High-throughput, Monte Carlo simulations parameterized from first-principles calculations coupled with experimental caloriemetry, neutron scattering and in situ microscopy
papers.findings: Reproduced key intermetallic phase formation and microstructural evolution features over varying temperatures. The technique captured transitions including liquidus behavior and ordering phenomena, lending confidence in predicting phase evolution in systems with sparse experimental data.
papers.mechanism: Utilizes chemical ordering models (via Monte Carlo) and fundamental Gibbs free energy minimization (G = H – T·S) to describe phase stability, where both enthalpy of formation and configurational entropy play decisive roles.

papers.title: Thermal Analysis of High-Entropy Rare Earth Oxides.
papers.system: High-entropy rare earth sesquioxides in equimolar compositions (e.g., La,Sm,Dy,Er,RE with RE = Nd, Gd, Y)
papers.approach: Splat quenching from the melt, high-temperature differential thermal analysis (DTA), and laser melting combined with synchrotron X-ray diffraction; supported by Calphad modeling
papers.findings: Measured fusion enthalpy, volume changes at melting, and determined melting points (e.g., 2456 ± 12 °C for (La,Sm,Dy,Er,Nd)2O3) which were higher than those of constituent oxides. The results are consistent with trends in pure rare earth sesquioxides and validate nonideal mixing effects.
papers.mechanism: Phase transitions are governed by nonideal mixing in both the solid and liquid states. Calphad modeling supports the experimental determination of thermodynamic parameters, linking volume changes and enthalpy of fusion.

papers.title: Thermal and Structural Analysis of a High-Entropy Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P20 Alloy-Infl
papers.approach: Differential scanning calorimetry (DSC) measurements during controlled heating and cooling to capture endothermic (melting) and exothermic (crystallization) events
papers.findings: Identified two distinct endothermic peaks during heating corresponding to pre-melting (∼1200 K) and definitive melting (∼1320 K) with quantified energy absorption values. DSC curves during cooling confirmed crystallization behavior, offering clues to enthalpy and, by integration, entropy changes associated with fusion.
papers.mechanism: The melting process is characterized by distinct thermal events where energy absorption corresponds to changes in atomic structure and phase; integration of cp(T) yields entropy change, thereby providing an approach to quantify fusion parameters.

papers.title: Microstructure and Thermal Analysis of Metastable Intermetallic Phases in High-Entropy Alloy CoCrFeMo0.85Ni.
papers.approach: Thermal analysis using differential thermal analysis (DTA) and differential scanning calorimetry (DSC) combined with microstructural and EDX studies
papers.findings: Determined phase-transition temperatures including solidus and liquidus, and measured enthalpy changes associated with melting and intermetallic formation. Identified discrepancies between CALPHAD-predicted and experimentally measured transition temperatures, emphasizing the need for precise thermal characterization.
papers.mechanism: Thermal events correspond to specific phase transformations where enthalpy changes (endothermic/exothermic peaks) denote the start of melting, crystallization or intermetallic transformations. This information is critical to compute related entropy changes using the Gibbs free energy framework.

papers.title: Third-Generation Thermodynamic Descriptions for Ta-Cr and Ta-V Binary Systems.
papers.system: Binary Ta-Cr and Ta-V systems (pure elements and their liquid and A2 phase behavior)
papers.approach: Development of advanced Gibbs energy models that incorporate thermal vacancies and detailed heat capacity (Cp) computations across a wide temperature range, using a two-state model for liquid phase properties
papers.findings: Achieved excellent agreement between calculated Cp curves and experimental data from 0 K up to 6000 K. The reliable description of both solid and liquid Gibbs energies, including thermal vacancy effects, supports accurate prediction of melting behavior.
papers.mechanism: The approach is based on a two-state model that captures the transition from solid to liquid by incorporating both the enthalpic contribution and thermal vacancy concentration, ensuring lattice stability over the entire temperature range.

papers.title: In-Situ Imaging of Molten High-Entropy Alloys Using Cold Neutrons.
papers.system: High-entropy alloys (e.g., CoCrCu and their mixtures with Ni) with emphasis on liquid-phase miscibility
papers.approach: In-situ neutron imaging using a high-temperature furnace and a neutron beam to capture real-time melt separation and alloying processes during melting and solidification
papers.findings: Successfully imaged the in-situ mixing, separation and eventual homogenization of liquids (e.g., Ni acting as a solubility pathway in CoCrCu) during melting; demonstrates that neutron imaging can reveal dynamic liquid-phase behavior in HEAs.
papers.mechanism: Contrast in neutron transmission between different elemental constituents enables visualization of phase separation and mixing at high temperatures, correlating with the underlying thermodynamic driving forces for miscibility.

papers.title: The Effect of Zr Addition on Melting Temperature, Microstructure, Recrystallization and Mechanical Properties of a Cantor High Entropy Alloy.
papers.system: Cantor alloy (CoCrFeMnNi) and its Zr-modified derivative
papers.approach: Vacuum induction melting combined with microstructural characterization (XRD, SEM) and thermal analysis
papers.findings: Found that the addition of Zr lowers the melting temperature (through eutectic formation with other elements) and refines the microstructure. This suggests that alloying additions can be used to tailor melting temperatures and liquid-phase behavior.
papers.mechanism: Eutectic reactions between Zr and other elements reduce the overall energy required for melting, thereby lowering the melting point while also influencing kinetics of homogenization during rapid melting.

papers.title: Thermodynamics-Guided High-Throughput Discovery of Eutectic High-Entropy Alloys for Rapid Solidification.
papers.system: Eutectic high-entropy alloys across a multicomponent compositional space
papers.approach: High-throughput CALPHAD modeling combined with empirical screening (using δr and VEC criteria) and subsequent solute trapping evaluations to predict phase constituents and melting-related behavior
papers.findings: Identified compositional regimes where eutectic mixtures form and provided predictive insights for the occurrence of amorphous phases versus structured eutectics, with emphasis on liquid–solid interface dynamics during rapid solidification.
papers.mechanism: Phase stability is determined through evaluation of Gibbs free energy contributions from enthalpy and configurational entropy under rapid solidification conditions, reinforcing the importance of both kinetic and thermodynamic factors.

established: DSC/DTA measurements can accurately capture heat capacity changes, endothermic/exothermic peaks and hence quantify thermal enthalpy, entropy and melting transitions.
MD and hybrid MC/MD simulations using reliable potentials (e.g., 2NN MEAM) are effective in modeling microscopic melting mechanisms and capturing grain size effects.

CALPHAD modeling, when combined with high-throughput experimental screening, provides a quantitative framework for predicting phase stability and melting temperatures in complex multicomponent systems.
In-situ neutron imaging offers a complementary method to visualize dynamic liquid-phase behavior, particularly miscibility and phase separation.

approaches_tried.approach: MD simulations (2NN MEAM) for tracking density, enthalpy, and structural rearrangements
approaches_tried.outcome: Identified two-stage melting processes and established grain-size–dependent melting point trends

approaches_tried.approach: DSC/DTA experiments measuring cp(T) over broad temperature ranges
approaches_tried.outcome: Determined thermal entropy and enthalpy changes, capturing melting and crystallization events effectively

approaches_tried.approach: CALPHAD modeling to predict phase diagrams and melting behavior
approaches_tried.outcome: Provided consistent predictions of melting points, fusion enthalpies, and liquidus/solidus boundaries, albeit with some discrepancies that highlight sensitivity to thermodynamic databases

approaches_tried.approach: Hybrid MC/MD simulations to follow thermodynamic evolution during annealing
approaches_tried.outcome: Captured convergence in free energy with quantification of enthalpy and entropy contributions

approaches_tried.approach: In-situ neutron imaging to visualize liquid-phase miscibility
approaches_tried.outcome: Demonstrated real-time observation of melt separation and alloying, providing qualitative support for thermodynamic models

mechanisms: Local atomic rearrangements and collective melting initiated at grain boundaries (premelting) followed by bulk melting.
Contributions of configurational versus thermal entropy in stabilizing the solid solution phase.
Eutectic reactions and nonideal mixing effects that lower melting points and modify fusion enthalpy.
Interplay between enthalpic contributions (from bond energy changes and formation energies) and entropic contributions determining the Gibbs free energy across phases.
disagreements: CALPHAD predictions sometimes show discrepancies with experimental phase transition temperatures, especially in complex HEAs where high-order interactions are not fully captured.
Uncertainty in quantitatively estimating the entropy of fusion from DSC data owing to overlapping contributions from configurational and thermal sources.
open_questions: How to develop a high-throughput yet accurate framework that can simultaneously capture melting temperature, fusion enthalpy, fusion entropy, volume changes at melting, and liquid-phase properties across a vast compositional space in HEAs.
What are the limits of current MD potentials and CALPHAD databases in describing liquid-phase behavior and phase transitions in multicomponent systems?
How to decisively validate the theoretical/simulation predictions with experimental methods in a manner that rules out the proposed approaches?
opportunities: Combining high-throughput DSC/DTA experiments with MD simulations to develop calibrated models for phase transitions in HEAs.
Integrating CALPHAD modeling with in-situ imaging techniques (e.g., cold neutron imaging) to provide both quantitative and qualitative validation of liquid-phase thermodynamics.
Exploring new multi-scale approaches that couple atomistic simulation (MD/MC), mesoscale phase-field models, and thermodynamic databases to cover both kinetic and equilibrium aspects of melting.

Conducting decisive validation experiments (e.g., precise measurement of volume changes at melting using synchrotron XRD under controlled conditions) to rule out models that fail to capture key liquid-phase behavior.

directions.direction: High-throughput calorimetry combined with in-situ synchrotron XRD to directly measure melting temperature, latent heat, entropy, and volume changes during melting
directions.assessment: Direct thermodynamic measurements by DSC/DTA coupled with structure-sensitive synchrotron XRD can yield high resolution data on phase‐transitions. This approach leverages well‐established DSC and XRD techniques (supported by PMC7513177::web::004::1_introduction and PMC11642357::web::012::3_results) and applies them in a high-throughput manner across HEA compositions. It directly addresses the need for accurate experimental fusion properties, though its applicability might be limited for highly segregated systems.

directions.direction: Advanced molecular dynamics simulations using machine-learning-enhanced interatomic potentials to predict fusion properties
directions.assessment: State-of-the-art MD methods, especially when enhanced with machine learning potentials calibrated against calorimetry data, can simulate melting behavior (e.g., abrupt density drop, grain-boundary premelting as in PMC8956691::web::012::results_and_discussion). This method directly probes the atomic mechanisms underlying fusion and can be efficient across compositions, though its accuracy depends on potential calibration.

directions.direction: Integration of CALPHAD modelling with in-situ neutron imaging to extract liquid-phase thermodynamic properties and volume changes
directions.assessment: CALPHAD provides a quantitative framework for phase stability and melting parameters (PMC7412006::web::014::2_7_calphad_modeling), and coupling it with neutron imaging (PMC8320920::web::018::5_conclusions) enables real-time visualization of liquid-phase behavior. This integrated approach penetrates liquid diffusivity and miscibility, directly targeting the challenge of liquid-phase property determination, although it requires sufficient neutron contrast.

directions.direction: Hybrid Monte Carlo/Molecular Dynamics simulations calibrated with high-throughput calorimetric screening to map fusion thermodynamic properties across vast compositional spaces
directions.assessment: MC/MD hybrid methods (PMC7921137::web::027::conclusion) are effective in capturing configurational and thermal contributions to melting while high-throughput DSC can validate the predictions. This approach is comprehensive and efficient for a wide range of compositions, though convergence and calibration uncertainties may arise.
